column1: # The conformance matrix: one row per conformance point of the Federation Tier
# with AQL specification, section 17, in specification order, so that each
# executed test records the points it exercised (section 16.4, #41).
# Tab-separated; lines starting with # are comments.
# Derived columns, never edited by hand: cp, actor, requirements, tracks. They
# come from the vendored conformance.adoc through
# `scripts/checks/conformance-matrix.sh` fails when a fresh derivation differs.
#   covered       at least one test carries the point's marker and CI runs it
#   planned       no test yet; issue names the work (allowed until #89)
#   deferred      a Gateway point not scored yet; needs an issue and a reason
#   node-profile  a Node point, scored against the member CDRs in the harness, never the gateway (section 16.2)
#   operator      an Operator point, verified at admission or in the registry
# Deferral authority (no specification governs this: our own design): only the
# owner defers a Gateway point, by a decision recorded on the issue the row
# names. A session may propose a deferral on that issue and never applies one.
# The reason cites the specification's own optionality (MAY, provisional,
# section 18) or an open blocking issue.
# The marker on a test is one line directly above its #[test] or
# #[tokio::test] attribute, naming CP ids and tracks only:

column7: reason

scored over two mock nodes: POST {base}/v1/query/aql and its ITS-REST GET form, and the GET forms of stored query execution with and without a version, send each node the same request and answer the same RESULT_SET; the query string is decoded by the generated openehr-its parameters, and one it refuses is a 400 that asks nobody

scored over three mock nodes with a localizer stub and the development cross-reference: a member the localizer does not name is not-localized and never asked, a localizer that is down or silent past its budget fails closed with its error on every member and in meta.federation, and ask-all on failure holds only where declared and is declared in OPTIONS

the status codes are scored (section 11.2, section 11.3); the OperationOutcome clause has no FHIR-facing consumer to apply to on an ITS-REST gateway, whose answer is a RESULT_SET with its additions under meta.federation only (N17, section 9.1, section 11.4)

section 12.3 and N22 route a version read on creating_system_id, while section 12a.1 route-ehr, section 12.5.1 and N41 route every request under a path ehr_id by that ehr_id; FerroFED follows N41, and the contradiction is recorded on #212

scored over two mock nodes: a versioned write naming its preceding version in If-Match, or in the path of a composition DELETE, reaches only the node its path ehr_id routes to, and only when the registry routes that version's creating_system_id there as the member's own system_id or a registered mapping; otherwise it is refused 409 and no node is sent it, a holder the map learned included; a versioned write naming no single version is refused 400; a new EHR with no target, or naming two endpoints, is refused 400 and never probed; a CONTRIBUTION is held to the same rule for every preceding_version_uid its body names, read with the ITS-REST NewContribution type and forwarded byte-identical, so one version another member controls refuses it 409 and no node is sent it, a CONTRIBUTION of creations alone routes by its path ehr_id, and a body that is no canonical-JSON CONTRIBUTION is refused 400; a PUT of an ehr_id a resolution binding or the ehr_id index places at another member than the targeted one is refused 409 ehr-id-held and no node is sent it, one at the member that holds it is forwarded for that node's own 409, and an ehr_id nothing places is forwarded and then indexed at the targeted member

scored over mock nodes through the real configuration path: a federated query, a routed read and write, a definition request, the ask-all probe, a stored-query definition and the admission check's EHR calls each reach their node with one openEHR-federation-client token, an ES384 JWS signed with the key the gateway publishes as federation.auth.jwks_uri, its aud the node's endpoint_id, exp at most 60 s after iat, naming the caller the guard verified (sub, iss_upstream, verified_by, the organisation, the purpose of use and the scopes as granted) and never the caller's own token; a caller claim carrying the patient identifier stops the request unsent, and a request with no verified caller reaches no node

the onward half is scored against the harness token endpoint and mock nodes: the gateway obtains a token with the client-credentials grant and an ES384 RFC 7523 client assertion the endpoint verifies against the JWK Set the gateway publishes and declares as federation.auth.jwks_uri, the node receives that token and never the caller token, a rotation publishes both keys for its overlap window, a token is cached until 30 s before it expires and dropped on a 401, and a token that cannot be obtained fails that node as node-error with nothing sent; the inbound half is scored over mock nodes: every caller presents an RFC 9068 token verified by key set or introspection, each failure (signature, issuer, audience, expiry, clock skew, algorithm, type, key, scope, purpose of use, an unreachable issuer) is refused before any node is asked, and the caller token never reaches a node
a Node obligation, scored against the member nodes of the harness and never the gateway (section 16.2); no specification governs the choice of two FerroEHR nodes: our own design
a Node obligation, scored against the member nodes of the harness and never the gateway (section 16.2); no specification governs the choice of two FerroEHR nodes: our own design
verified at admission or in the registry, not on a request (section 16.2); the gateway assists: its registry load refuses an endpoint whose connectionType is hl7-fhir-rest or no defined code

the body, the endpoint list without a patient identifier, the sub-path Allow, and each its_rest area declaration held to the behaviour of that area in every mode are scored, and so is the clause that the endpoint list is subject to the gateway normal authentication (section 7a.2, section 13): OPTIONS {base}/ answers 401 without a token

scored over mock nodes on the routed path and on the federated AQL answer: a request routed or dispatched to one endpoint, by a directive, a header or a patient resolving at one member alone, names it and its system_id whatever it answered; a fan-out lists the endpoints that contributed rows and their system_ids in registry order, comma-separated as the section 8.4 request header, and a failing answer or a node with no rows is not listed

scored over two mock nodes in both modes: by default a read and a create answer 501 and no node is asked; with federation.demographic_endpoint set a request naming that endpoint reaches it alone, byte-identical and with the N31 provenance headers, while a request naming no endpoint is refused 400 target-required and one naming another endpoint, several endpoints or * is refused 400, and no node is asked; an endpoint the registry does not hold refuses the configuration; OPTIONS its_rest.demographic declares each mode and the behaviour matches it
a Node obligation, scored against the member nodes of the harness and never the gateway (section 16.2); no specification governs the choice of two FerroEHR nodes: our own design

the stored-query clause is scored on a query stored at the gateway and invoked by name, targeted by the header and by the directive with the same answer, and refused 400 when the two select different node sets (section 8.4, section 12.7)

scored over two mock nodes with node A behind the capturing proxy: a version node A created and node B holds as an import is one row under version-identity, read from node A with node B suppressed in meta.federation.dedup; a write against it through node B's ehr_id, routed by the ehr_id index or the targeting header, is refused 409 naming the creating_system_id and node A's endpoint whether node A refuses connections or answers, node B is sent nothing and node A is never tried; a write through node A's own ehr_id reaches node A alone and its answer names node A and no copy

the routing clause is scored (explicit target, binding, index, then a read-only ask-all, and a write no earlier step routes refused 400 and never probed), and so is the integrity clause over two mock nodes: an ehr_id a binding, the index or the probe finds at two members is a 409 listing them on a read as on a write, neither is sent the request, one integrity incident is logged per refusal, and the index-insert alarm of section 12b.2 fires once; a binding collision is scored on the routing order alone until client sessions exist (#80), and the two-node harness of tracks 6 and 11 is #91; two creates racing for one ehr_id at two members raise the index-insert alarm once

verified at admission or in the registry, not on a request (section 16.2); the gateway assists: ferrofed admission check reports each identifier-integrity condition of section 12b.2 as pass, fail or cannot-check with its evidence, and the registry load refuses a second member with an existing system_id

scored over two mock nodes: every template and stored-query definition request reaches the one endpoint the targeting headers name, byte-identical, and is answered as that node answered, its 4xx included; without a target, with *, an unknown id or several ids it is refused 400 and no node is asked; a template list is one node's answer, never a union; with the registry offered, stored queries stay at the gateway while templates route; without the registry both stored-query PUTs route, the versioned one included, and every forwarded body carries a Content-Type its operation declares (#298); the fan-out upload clauses are scored over three mock nodes with federation.fan_out_template_upload on (off by default, declared in OPTIONS): a template upload naming * or several endpoints reaches each member byte-identical and is answered per node in the meta.federation shape, 207 with complete false when one member rejects or times out, the accepting members keep the template and are never sent a rollback, 200 only when every named member accepted, 424 when none did, a failing member reported with its HTTP status and an excerpt of its message, no other node body copied; a plain upload still names its one node, and * stays a 400 on every other definition request and whenever the setting is off (#76)
verified at admission or in the registry, not on a request (section 16.2)

the registry clauses are scored: invocation by name over more than one member with name and endpoints[], the refused second PUT, also between two gateways racing one new version over one shared PostgreSQL store with exactly one stored (e2e, #268), a read-only registry answering PUT 405, and a directed definition stored and executed federated; the definition fan-out clauses are scored over three mock nodes with federation.fan_out_stored_queries on (off by default, refused by config check without the registry, declared in OPTIONS only beside it; with it off, a registry PUT or version GET carrying a targeting header is a 400 storing and reading nothing): a PUT naming * is stored at the registry first and reaches each member as the registry's canonical AQL, 207 with complete false when one member fails and 424 when all do, nothing rolled back and the registry's version standing, a failing member reported with its HTTP status and an excerpt of its message, no other node body copied; a FROM ENDPOINT or ORGANISATION definition is a 400 before anything is stored and stays storable and executable federated; an invocation dispatches the registry's AQL inline even where a member holds a differing copy; a GET of a version naming * reports per member a matching copy as active and a differing or missing one as node-error with a code (#78); every second PUT of a held version is 409 and reaches no node, the same query naming members included, and drift is repaired by the operator on the admin listener (present only with metrics.listen, loopback unless allow_remote), whose POST sends the held copy to the named members on the same statuses with meta.registry held and leaves the registry's copy unchanged, reaching a member that missed the first distribution or was admitted after it (#342)
